privacy: Welcome to our Privacy Notice, designed to inform you about how we handle your personal data following the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) when you use our website featuring the GenAI Reward Machine.

To make the subject matter of this notice clearer, let us define some terms from the GDPR. The "controller" refers to us, as we decide how and why your personal data is used, which also makes us responsible for protecting your personal data. "Personal data" includes any information that can identify you directly or indirectly, like your IP address. "Processing" covers all actions done with your data, such as collecting, storing, using, and deleting it.
It is important to read this notice to understand what data we collect from you, why we collect it, what we do with it, and what rights you have regarding your data.
If you have any questions about this notice, please reach out to the controller:
**Dr. Nicolas Pope**,
**Postal address:** University of Eastern Finland, Länsikatu 15, 80110 Joensuu, Finland.
**Email:** nicolas.pope@uef.fi
### 1. Data Processing Activity:
We log IP addresses.
However, we do not use cookies for tracking or analytics; instead, we provide content based solely on your inputs.
### 2. Purposes of Processing:
Logging IP addresses helps maintain website integrity and security by identifying and preventing malicious activities.
### 3. Legal Basis for Processing:

Primarily, we process IP addresses for security reasons, based on our legitimate interest in protecting our website and data as per Article 6(1)(f) GDPR. Again, we may also process data based on your consent under Article 6(1)(a) GDPR if you would like to exercise your right to access your logged IP address. In addition, we may process your personal data if we are instructed to do so by a competent court under Article 6(1)(c).
### 4. Legitimate Interests Pursued:
Our goal is to keep the website running by maintaining website integrity, and security, and preventing abuse.
### 5. Security:
We implement security measures to protect your IP addresses from unlawful access or damage. Your IP addresses are encrypted during any subsequent transfer.
### 6. Data Recipients:
Only authorized website personnel can access your IP address for security and maintenance purposes.
### 7. Data Transfers:
IP addresses may be transferred to Microsoft servers, but we ensure GDPR compliance for data protection.
### 8. Storage Limitation:
We keep IP addresses only as long as necessary, typically up to 7 days, unless required by law.
### 9. Your Rights:
Under GDPR, you have rights including

* Right to be informed: In addition to informing, you about processing purposes, retention periods, and to whom your data is shared, you have the right to be informed on how we collect. We collect your IP address when you visit our website.
* Right to access: you can request a copy of your logged IP address and associated log data.

* Right to rectification: if the logged data is inaccurate or incomplete, you can request rectification although IP address is not typically something that can be corrected in the same way as other data.
* Right to erasure: you can request deletion of your IP address within 7 days of your last visit to this website since your address is deleted automatically after 7 days.
* Right to object: you can object to the processing of your IP addresses.
* Right to lodge a complaint: you can lodge a complaint to the supervisory authority if you think that your data is not processed following GDPR provisions.
### 10. Updates to This Privacy Notice:
We may update this notice to reflect changes in our data processing practices or legal requirements. We will notify you of any changes.
We value your privacy and we are committed to protect your data and ensuring GDPR compliance. If you have questions or want to exercise your rights, contact us at nicolas.pope@uef.fi.

tooltip.exploit: Exploitation: Prefer actions with the highest estimated reward.
tooltip.explore: Exploration: Occasionally try random actions to discover potentially better strategies.
tooltip.smallAlpha: Low learning rate: Learn slowly by making only small updates from new experiences.
tooltip.largeAlpha: High learning rate: Learn quickly by making large updates from new experiences.
tooltip.smallGamma: Low discount factor: Future rewards have little influence when updating learned values.
tooltip.largeGamma: High discount factor: Future rewards have a strong influence when updating learned values.

hud.agentVis: This observation view visualizes the observation received by the agent from the environment and combines it with the Q-values stored and updated by the agent. Actual observation in this game is not images but just numbers. Q-values, the values that represent expected reward from action, are stored paired to the state values.
hud.alpha: The learning rate controls how quickly the agent learns from new experiences. A higher value changes learned Q-values more after each update, while a lower value changes them more gradually.
hud.gamma: The discount factor controls how much future rewards affect learning. A higher value makes the agent learn with long-term rewards in mind, while a lower value focuses learning more on immediate rewards.
hud.epsilon: The exploration rate controls how often the agent tries a random action instead of the best action it currently knows. Random actions help the agent discover better strategies.
hud.qTable: This map visualizes the Q-Table of Q-learning agent. You can zoom and pan around. Focus on to current observation with button on the right side of this frame. When in fast-mode, it shows lower resolution
hud.stats: See how the reward and win/lose rate progress

inspect.0: This is the current observation. Q-value of action taken in this state will be updated based on the reward received when reaching next state, while considering also how good that state is by its' previous learning.
inspect.1: These are the Q-values for each action. Click markers to see actual values.
inspect.2: Agent picks action that has highest Q-value. Inspect what could it be? Agent may also take random action with probability of "Epsilon" or as simplified, curiosity in this game.
inspect.3: This is the reward agent received from the environment: REWARD HERE
inspect.4: And this is the new state the agent has reached. Click markers to see actual values.
inspect.5:
Q-value for action that was taken is updated by adjusting it with following formula: adjustment = alpha * (reward + gamma * maxNext - old Q-value) 
 Those greek letters are translated in this game following: alpha = Adaptability, gamma = Foresight
inspect.6: This was the previous state. Click on marker to see how it was updated.
inspect.7: Click Inspect again at any point of the game to run these 8 steps again.

text.1: Hi, and welcome to Reward Machine!
text.2: In this level, the goal is the treasure chest.
text.3: First, you will design your agent and learn how to play the game.
text.4: Your tasks are shown on the left. Complete them all, and "Test" button will appear. Your agent then has to succesfully complete the level without interference.
text.5: First, choose how your agent looks. Open the "Agent" menu and change its appearance.
text.6: Clock up there shows how many moves the agent has left. The agent itself does not know how much time is left. The agent must reach the goal before time run out.
text.7: Now let's start the game. You can play one step at a time.
text.8: Or let the agent play continuously.
text.9: You can also let the agent play at unlimited speed. This helps it learn quickly!
text.10: Use Fast Forward to speed up learning.
text.11: Great! Fast Forward helps the agent learn quickly. In later levels, you will get to change what the agent learns and see how it learns.
text.12: All tasks are complete! Click "Test Agent" in the progress panel. To pass the level, the agent must reach the goal 5 times.

1.nextLevelInfo: The next level will introduce you to the concept of rewards. The agent learns from the rewards it receives while playing and remembers which actions were rewarded the most in different situations.
1.postMessage: In this level, you learned how the game works. You taught your agent to reach the goal successfully! In reinforcement learning, an agent learns by playing and interacting with the game.
1.preMessage: In reinforcement learning, an agent learns by playing and interacting with the game. Your goal is to teach your agent how to play. First, complete the tasks to set up the game and help your agent learn. Then, test your agent to see if it has learned to complete the level.

text.1: First, let's recap. Reach the goal. Again, the treasure chest is the goal.
text.2: That was easy! But from now on, you need also teach the agent to collect score on the way.
text.3: You can see your score next to the clock. Your objective is to beat the high score!
text.4: For that, you need to teach the agent to avoid the mushrooms and other traps...
text.5: ...and collect the small and big treasures!
text.6: Next, tune the rewards so the agent avoids mushrooms and collects treasures while still reaching the goal in time.
text.7: You can set the reward for when the agent runs out of time before reaching the goal.
text.8: And you can set the rewards for reaching different items.
text.9: Complete all tasks and test your agent to complete the level!

2.nextLevelInfo: Agent already learnt a lot. But how much is enough? The agent must try new things to learn new things but also it has to settle for something. Next level will introduce you to exploration vs exploitation dilemma.
2.postMessage: In this level, you learned that the agent receives rewards from the environment in different situations.
2.preMessage: In this level, your goal is to tune the rewards for treasures and traps so that the agent avoids traps, collects treasures, and reaches the goal in time. Remember, the agent always tries to maximize its reward. It does not know the actual goal or the tasks.

text.1: Again, your agent needs to reach to the goal. This time there is three possible goals to choose. Agent should also receive at least one point to beat the level.
text.2: The agent should explore more and not exploit its' best knowledge of the level so much.
text.3: This problem is called exploration-explotation dilemma.
text.4: Luckily for us, there is a parameter that we can tune to overcome this issue!
text.5: In this game it is called "Curiosity".
text.6: This parameter tunes how often agent selects random action on instead of best action it knows.
text.7: Usually 0.1 (10% propability!) is enough, but in this level you may need keep it higher for at least some time that your agent explores enough.
text.8: Good luck! You can reset agents memory from trash button near agent menu. BTW: For test phase the Curiosity is set to 0 and it follows the best learned policy.

3.nextLevelInfo: At the next level we take a glimpse how agent actually observes the environment. We also take a look to how it stores its' learned.
3.postMessage: This level taught you about exploration vs exploitation dilemma: The agent can not know what is the ultimate reward, but it has to stop looking at some point.
3.preMessage: In this level you hit to the exploration-explotation dilemma: Should the agent try more things to learn more or exploit already feasible policy.

text.1: There are two things in this level: 1. the observation and 2. how it values future rewards, also known as "discounted rewards".
text.2: Let's start with the observation. The agent can observe the environment. In this game, the agent can only observe part of the whole environment, or as we say in reinforcement learning: "Partial Observation." Well, enough with the technical stuff. Let's have a look...
text.3: This new inspection tool is called "Agent Vision." It allows you to clearly see what the agent actually observes.
text.4: And yeah, the agent actually doesn't see or observe the game. It just receives numbers representing these tiles. Toggle it to see the agent's actual observation with that button in the frame.
text.5: That's that. Now for your task in this level!
text.6: You already know that the agent receives rewards from the environment.
text.7: These rewards help the agent learn. But sometimes, it needs to think about future rewards too, not just the reward it gets right now.
text.8: For example, an action might give a small negative reward now, but lead to a much bigger reward later.
text.9: Your agent playing there might have already learned to just avoid progressing past those mushrooms. The agent needs to learn some foresight. But how?
text.10: Luckily for us, there is a parameter for that too! In this game, it is called "Foresight."
text.11: This parameter controls how much the agent values where an action may lead, even if the immediate reward is low.
text.12: The agent needs to receive at least one point to beat the level.
text.13: Good luck! You might gain some help by tuning the "Curiosity" higher at first and then gradually decaying it to a smaller value.

4.nextLevelInfo: Next, we dig deeper and see how the learning actually happens!
4.postMessage: This level taught you about observations and how an agent can use foresight to consider future rewards.
4.preMessage: In this level, we will think more about rewards and how the agent learns from them. The agent should consider future rewards, not just immediate ones. Otherwise, it may not learn to choose actions that lead to better rewards later. You will also learn about the agent's observations and see the game from the agent's point of view.

text.0: Hi! And welcome to creating your own Reinforcement Learning game!
text.1: In this game, you will create an agent and then an environment for it to play in!
text.2: Let's start by choosing how your agent looks!
text.3: Next, you need to select the observation shape.
text.4: Great! You can come back and make changes later if you like. Your agent also has a few parameters that we will tune later, but let's not worry about those yet.
text.5: Okay! Now it's time to work on the environment. Start by designing the tools you will use to build it.
text.6: Start by creating a new tile tool for walls.
text.7: Good! Now create a tile tool for the spawn area. Tiles painted with this tool will mark where the agent can spawn.
text.8: Nice! Now create a tile to represent your agent's goal. Think about your story. Maybe your agent is searching for a chest full of gold, or looking for butterflies while avoiding spiders and bugs? Your world, your choice!
text.9: You can make your world more interesting by creating a few more tile tools, if you like.
text.10: Now it's time to build your world. Open the toolbox. To modify your world, select a tile tool from the list and click where you want to place it. To continue, you need to add at least one Goal tile.
text.11: The last things to set for your game are the round length and the game name!
text.12: Great! Your game is ready. You can save it from the game settings. Remember, you can always come back and change your world and choices.
text.13: Next, you can change how the agent is rewarded for its actions.
text.14: These are the rewards you can change. They are already set up quite well, but come back later and adjust them to change the agent's behaviour.
text.15: Great! Let's start playing. This bar shows what you have collected and your current score.
text.16: And here are the controls. Click Play to start the game!
text.17: Nice! The agent has started to act in the environment. Let's take a look at what it observes.
text.18: Okay, this is the agent's observation. It is visualized here to show what the agent can see. Use the "Step" button to move forward one step at a time and see how the observation changes.
text.19: The agent actually receives something different from these images. Click the "Agent View" button to see what the agent actually receives.
text.20: These are the actual numbers your agent receives. For example, you created "Solid" tiles, which the agent sees as number 1. For a "Spawn" tile, it receives number -1, and for a "Goal" tile, it receives number 2.
text.21: Okay, so that's what the agent observes. You can now start the game again and change the game speed using the controls.
text.22: The tutorial continues when you have reached the goal 10 times. This may take some time. The Fast Forward button should get you there in seconds. If reaching the goal is really difficult, try making your world easier.
text.23: Great! The agent has reached the goal 10 times. It should have already learned something.
text.24: The agent learns from the rewards it receives. It learns which actions are good or bad in different states. Let's take a closer look.
text.25: This shows what the agent has learned so far. It keeps track of how useful different actions are in different situations.
text.26: The agent updates what it has learned after each action, based on the reward it receives and what it expects to happen next.
text.27: How does this work? Let's take a closer look. Click the "Inspect" button.
text.32: Here are the Curiosity and Foresight settings mentioned in the Inspect view. You can change how the agent learns by adjusting them.
text.33: You don't need to fully understand the formula or how each change affects learning. You can also just try different settings and see what happens.
text.34: Just a few more things! This is the last part of the game. Here you can see how the agent's learning is progressing.
text.35: You obtain score by collecting Score +1, Score +2 and lose it if agent encounters Score -1. Score only counts for episodes that end at the goal. If time runs out, your score is 0.
text.36: Score is completely different from rewards. Your score is used to show how well you did and to let you compete with other players.
text.37: That's it! To start the tutorial again, go to the homepage and refresh your browser. Click Next to start playing.

stageInfo.basic: In reinforcement learning, an agent learns by playing and interacting with the game. Your goal is to teach your agent how to play. First, complete the tasks to set up the game and help your agent learn. Then, test your agent to see if it has learned to complete the level.

agentBubble.3: Yep! In AI, an agent is something that acts on behalf of someone or something by observing and making decisions.
agentBubble.4: In this game, I'm one of the available agents and act like a computer-controlled character.
agentBubble.5: I'm actually a Q-learning agent, but let's not go there yet. You can just call me Robodog Agent! 😎
agentBubble.6: In this tutorial game, my task is to learn to defend my home from a burglar, while avoiding making a mess by bumping into flower pots.
agentBubble.7: I have partial observation of my environment, meaning I can only see a small part of my home at each turn, or timestep as we call them 😎
agentBubble.8: This is what I can see, my observation!
agentBubble.9: I can see one step in each direction, and I can also sense which direction the burglar is in. Looks like he's on the right side!
agentBubble.10: In this game you can see the whole environment (my home), and the state it is in, but I only observe the white area around me and the direction of the burglar.
agentBubble.11: The thing is, I don't actually know much at the beginning. In reinforcement learning, the agent usually starts without knowing what to do.
agentBubble.13: It means I learn by interacting with the environment and getting feedback.
agentBubble.15: When I do some action in this environment, I get a reward.
agentBubble.16: If I spook the burglar I get rewarded positively 💚, but if I break a pot or bark unnecessarily, I get a negative reward 💔
agentBubble.17: At the beginning I don't really know what I'm doing. I just try random actions and remember which ones worked better in each situation.
agentBubble.18: Let's try a few rounds, or episodes as we call them 😎
agentBubble.20: Ouch! ☹️ So when there was a flower pot on that side, it might not be a good idea to go there!
agentBubble.21: Okay, so no barking for no reason!
agentBubble.22: Hey! Yeah, I spooked the burglar away and got a nice reward!
agentBubble.23: But yeah, I'm an AI agent so let's speed things up...
agentBubble.26: Now no burglar can evade me! 😇

hints.concepts: These are the fundamental concepts of reinforcement learning that you'll encounter throughout the game.

1.title: What is Reinforcement Learning Agent?
1.option2: An AI that learns through interaction and feedback

2.title: What is Environment?
2.option1: The world in which the agent acts

3.title: How did the Robodog learn?
3.option1: It read a manual "How to win Pots and Burglars game"
3.option2: Robodog was pre-programmed for the task

recap.1: An agent is an AI that makes decisions and acts.
recap.2: The environment is the world the agent operates in and responds to the agent's actions.
recap.3: The task defines what the agent is trying to learn. In reinforcement learning, the agent learns by interacting with the environment and receiving feedback.
recap.4: At each timestep, the agent receives an observation from the environment. The state describes the full situation of the environment, but the agent often only sees part of it (the observation).
recap.5: The agent chooses an action that affects the environment. The environment returns a reward, which indicates how good or bad the action was for the task.
recap.6: An episode is one complete run from start to finish. During episodes, the agent learns which actions lead to better rewards in different situations.
recap.title: Recap
